2. Refuse with HoldNotAllowed. Nothing will ever come back for a title with no copies in circulation (all withdrawn, or none added).
3. Yes to both: one active hold per member per title, and a member who has a copy of that title on loan right now can't hold it. Both HoldNotAllowed.
4. I don't mind a cap or children placing holds; use your recommendation. Unknown member -> MemberNotFound, unknown ISBN -> TitleNotFound.

6. Yes, that's right: only the holder can take a set-aside copy, everyone else gets CopyNotAvailable. The holder's checkout follows the normal rules; if it's refused, the hold stays READY and the clock keeps running.
7. I don't mind; use your recommendation.
8. I don't mind; put it wherever you see fit.
9. Yes. Cancel works on WAITING or READY holds. A cancelled READY hold's copy moves on as in expiry (fresh window from today, or back to the shelf if nobody waits). Cancelling a non-active hold -> HoldNotAllowed; unknown id -> HoldNotFound.
10. Yes. A READY hold expires only once pickup_by is before today (the pickup day itself is still fine). WAITING holds never expire. A second run the same day expires nothing. The copy goes to the next waiting hold with a window of today + 7 (Monday if Sunday), or back to the shelf. For the roadmap items (the 5.00 block, the 1.00 no-show fee), go with what the roadmap says.
11. Yes: only WAITING and READY holds, in the order they were placed.
12. Fine, no change.

Also, for later, this is where the service is heading: renewals are next. Two rules will apply. s += '''

class HoldStatus(Enum):
    WAITING = "waiting"      # in the queue, no copy yet
    READY = "ready"          # a copy is on the hold shelf for the member
    FULFILLED = "fulfilled"  # the member borrowed the title
    CANCELLED = "cancelled"
    EXPIRED = "expired"      # set aside but not collected in time


ACTIVE_HOLD_STATUSES = frozenset({HoldStatus.WAITING, HoldStatus.READY})


@dataclass
class Hold:
    hold_id: str
    member_id: str
    isbn: str
    placed_on: date
    status: HoldStatus
    copy_id: str | None
    pickup_by: date | None

    @property
    def is_active(self) -> bool:
        return self.status in ACTIVE_HOLD_STATUSES
'''

p = pathlib.Path("src/lending/errors.py")
p.write_text(p.read_text() + '''

class HoldNotAllowed(LendingError):
    """A hold that can't be placed or changed in the current state."""

    def __init__(self, why: str) -> None:
        super().__init__(f"hold not allowed: {why}")
        self.why = why


class HoldNotFound(LendingError):
    def __init__(self, hold_id: str) -> None:
        super().__init__(f"no hold {hold_id!r}")
        self.hold_id = hold_id
''')

p = pathlib.Path("src/lending/policy.py")
p.write_text(p.read_text() + '''

# Holds -----------------------------------------------------------------

# A member owing this much or more cannot place a hold. Lower than the
# borrowing bar: a hold ties up a copy for someone who already owes.
HOLD_BLOCK_THRESHOLD = Decimal("5.00")

PICKUP_DAYS = 7

# Charged when a copy set aside for a hold is not collected in time.
NO_SHOW_FEE = Decimal("1.00")

# Categories that never pay the no-show fee.
NO_SHOW_EXEMPT: frozenset[MemberCategory] = frozenset({MemberCategory.CHILD})


def pickup_by(set_aside_on: date) -> date:
    """Last day to collect a held copy, never a closed day."""
    return next_open_day(set_aside_on + timedelta(days=PICKUP_DAYS))


def is_hold_blocked(balance: Decimal) -> bool:
    return balance >= HOLD_BLOCK_THRESHOLD
''')

p = pathlib.Path("src/lending/repository.py")

''')

    # holds -------------------------------------------------------------

    def add_hold(self, hold: Hold) -> None:
        self._holds[hold.hold_id] = hold

    def get_hold(self, hold_id: str) -> Hold:
        try:
            return self._holds[hold_id]

    def holds_on(self, isbn: str) -> list[Hold]:
        """Every hold ever placed on the title, in the order placed."""
        return [h for h in self._holds.values() if h.isbn == isbn]

    def all_holds(self) -> list[Hold]:
        return list(self._holds.values())
'''
p.write_text(s)
